cases.title: Resistive voltage divider (DC)
cases.purpose: 10 V across two 1 kOhm resistors. All three evidence sources must agree at 5.000 V: Invention Lab DC solver, Ngspice .op on the EXPORTED deck, and the analytical result.
modelNotes: Ideal resistors and sources. Both engines include gmin = 1e-12 ground leakage (SPICE default); it loads the midpoint by ~2.5e-9 V, so the analytical comparison uses abs 1e-7 V to cover the documented model choice rather than pretending both solvers are ideal-free.
cases.toleranceRationale: abs 1e-6 V: the network is linear and both solvers are direct eliminations; remaining differences are double-precision roundoff only.

cases.title: RC step response (transient, backward Euler vs Ngspice vs analytical)
cases.purpose: R=1 kOhm, C=100 nF, 0-to-5 V step (pulse train with first half-cycle high). Analytical tau = 100 microseconds. Compare the capacitor voltage at t = 0.5, 1, 2, 3 tau against Ngspice and the closed-form solution.
modelNotes: No UIC on either side: both start from the operating point with the source at 0 V, so vC(0) = 0 matches the declared initial condition.
cases.toleranceRationale: abs 0.005 V IL-vs-Ngspice (both integrators converged well below signal scale); abs 0.01 V IL-vs-analytical covers the documented O(dt) error of backward Euler at dt = tau/500. Rise-time caveat: Ngspice uses a 1 ns PWL rise (analytical assumes an ideal step); both are settled long before the first sample at 50 microseconds.

cases.title: Diode operating points at three bias levels (temperature-matched)
cases.purpose: Shockley diode (Is=1e-12, n=1) fed from 5 V through 1 kOhm, repeated at Vs = 3, 5, 10 V. Compare diode voltage against Ngspice and a bisection reference of the same equation. Temperature matched at T = 300.0 K via .options temp/tnom = 26.85 C so both engines use Vt = k*300/q exactly.
modelNotes: Both engines: Shockley equation I = Is*(exp(V/nVt) - 1), n=1, Is=1e-12, no series resistance, no breakdown. Temperature: 300.0 K on both sides (documented .options). The bisection reference is an independent numerical root-finder, not the same Newton implementation.
cases.toleranceRationale: abs 1e-4 V: Newton tolerance in both engines is far tighter (1e-9); gmin-style leakage conductance contributes < 1e-11 A here; the residual budget covers SPICE reltol=1e-3 propagating through the node voltage.

cases.title: NMOS transfer curve (saturation sweep) and linear-region point
cases.purpose: Sweep Vgs 0..5 V at Vds=5 V (all points saturated): drain current via a series ammeter, Invention Lab dcSweep vs Ngspice .dc on the exported deck. Plus a linear-region point (Vgs=3, Vds=1, LAMBDA=0).
modelNotes: Model equivalence (documented): KP*(W/L) with W=L=1u equals the internal k; VTO maps to vth; LAMBDA maps to lambda. W and L are declared as 1u/1u on the M line.

The internal engine applies (1+lambda*Vds) in saturation only; Ngspice Level-1 applies it in the linear region too. Benchmarks touching the linear region therefore use LAMBDA=0, where both reduce to the same law — a documented model nuance, not a hidden tolerance change.
Both sides: no body effect (bulk tied to source), no capacitances (DC analysis).
cases.toleranceRationale: series maxAbs 5e-4 A (0.5% of the 95 mA full-scale current): both engines implement the same Level-1 square law with W/L=1; the residual covers Newton/reltol differences. The linear-region point uses abs 1e-6 A because with LAMBDA=0 the two models reduce to identical equations.

cases.title: Combined nonlinear circuit: sine source, R-C divider, diode clamp
cases.purpose: Sine 2 V amplitude + 3 V offset at 1 kHz drives R1=1 kOhm into a node carrying C=100 nF to ground, R2=500 Ohm to ground, and a diode (Is=1e-12, n=1) clamping to ground. The diode conducts near the sine peaks, exercising nonlinear interaction. Compare the node voltage at 20 sample points over two periods.
modelNotes: All elements supported on both sides. The diode enters forward conduction near waveform peaks (both engines must show the same clamped shape).
cases.toleranceRationale: maxAbs 0.02 V and RMS 0.01 V (1-2% of signal): backward Euler (internal, dt=20us) vs Ngspice trapezoidal integration differ at O(dt) on a smooth waveform; temperature matched at 300 K for the diode; residual differences are documented discretization effects, not model mismatches.

checks.name: combined waveform IL vs Ngspice (19 points, t > 0)
diode clamp engaged (peak held below unclamped divider level)
checks.note: peak node voltage 0.566 V (unclamped would reach ~1.0 V)

notes: Initialization-convention difference (documented, t=0 excluded from comparison): IL v(A,0)=0.375 V (declared vInit=0, companion model active) vs Ngspice DC-operating-point t=0 0.544 V (capacitor open). Difference 0.169 V is a convention difference, not a solver defect; waveforms converge after the first tau.

verdictDoc.pass: Invention Lab and the independent reference agree within the documented tolerance.
verdictDoc.fail: A comparison exceeded its tolerance or an engine produced invalid data.
verdictDoc.skipped: The benchmark did not run (e.g. external engine unavailable). NEVER counted as a pass.
verdictDoc.unsupported: The benchmark targets behavior the platform explicitly does not support.
verdictDoc.model-mismatch: The two engines implement genuinely different mathematical models; documented, not a bug.
verdictDoc.inconclusive: The benchmark ran but the comparison cannot decide (e.g. missing tolerance).
